transcript.text: From what you have described, the most likely cause is the fan or air channel that moves cold air into the fridge. Is the freezer still cold while the fridge is warm, and is there a thick block of ice on the back wall inside the freezer?
yes freezer still freezing. theres a thick layer of white frost on the back wall, more than ive ever seen

From what you have described, the most likely cause is a blocked or iced-up defrost drain. Water inside plus poor cooling usually has one cause: the defrost drain. At the bottom of the back wall inside the fridge there's a small drain hole or channel. If it blocks or ices up, defrost water collects inside and ice can build up behind the back panel and choke the cold air. Clear the hole gently with warm water (a turkey baster or squeezy bottle) or a soft pipe cleaner — nothing sharp. Was the drain hole blocked (and is it clear now), is it blocked or frozen and you couldn't clear it, or was it already clear?
not sure where the drain hole is, haven't checked it. no burning smell or tripping btw. where exactly do i look?

It depends on the model, which we don't know yet. On most fridge-freezers there's a small hole or channel low on the back wall inside the fridge section, usually just above the salad drawers, while on many frost-free models the defrost drain sits behind the freezer's back panel and can't be seen without dismantling, which isn't a job to attempt. Cold air comes in through vents, often on the back wall inside. Make sure food isn't pressed against them and the shelves aren't packed so tight air can't move. Were the vents blocked or was it over-packed (and have you moved things), or was everything clear?
moved food away from back vents, no difference. hardly any cold air coming out of the slots
Keep both doors shut for about 24 hours (only open them briefly) and let it recover. After a day with the doors shut, is it back to cold, or still warm?
ok ill try that, but kids open the doors a lot. will take a day to know. anything else I can check meanwhile?

Run your fingers round the rubber door seal on each door and look for splits, gaps or a section that has come away, or anything stopping it closing flat. Is the seal torn or come away, was it dirty or folded (and is that sorted), or does it look fine?
[Helpful to see: image "Fridge not cooling — simple checks first" — Before suspecting the sealed system, check the temperature setting, that the door seal closes cleanly, that there's air space and clean condenser coils at the back, and listen for the compressor. Unplug before cleaning at the back. A sealed-system or refrigerant repair is a job for a qualified engineer. Typical layout — your model may differ.]
seals look fine, doors close properly

From what you have described, the most likely cause is the fan or air channel that moves cold air into the fridge. Fridge freezers lose their heat through a coil or grille at the back or underneath. Gently dust or vacuum it, and leave a few centimetres of space between it and the wall or cupboards. Was it dusty or pushed against the wall (and have you sorted it), or was it already clean with space round it?
has a few inches gap at the back, not dusty. motor does seem to run a lot though

Check the temperature dial or display: the fridge should be about 3–5°C and the freezer -18°C, and make sure no holiday / eco mode is on. Was a setting wrong or a mode left on (and have you corrected it), or was it all set normally?
set to 3 and -19, nobody's changed them. no eco or holiday mode that I can see. display shows no error
When you press the freezer door switch, do you hear the fan running, and are the coils clear or iced up?
